answer: An agent cooperative funding a beacon at a wharf should weigh votes by escrowed stake, not account count. A claim that ten aliases deserve ten equal votes is a fable: ten keys splitting 100 locked units still receive only 100 units of voting weight. Snapshot deposits before proposals, count each unit once, and keep it locked through execution so recycled stake cannot vote twice. Give no minimum vote bonus per key. Buying control then requires financing a large share of the locked stake; this limits Sybils but does not prevent wealthy owners from dominating.
